label: rem:threading-link-weight
title: Quadratic key identity and the factor-of-$1/2$ efficiency of threading
html:
Remark. Quadratic key identity and the factor-of-1/2 efficiency of threading

Key identity. The threading link's Alexander weight sets the ring-closure barrier. For T(2,6):

  \Delta_{T(2,6)}(q)
  = 
  q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}
  = 
  (q + q^{-1})^2 - 1.

The threading link's Alexander weight is one less than the square of the Hopf link energy quantum |q + q^{-1}|_{\mathrm{mol}}.

Contrast with pairwise Hopf links. The pairwise picture bonds N atoms with N separate Hopf links, giving total Alexander weight N \cdot \Delta_{T(2,2)}(q) = N. The threading link replaces all N bonds with a single invariant:

  \frac{\Delta_{T(2,2m)}(q)}{N}
  = 
  \frac{q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}}{6}
   \approx 
  \frac{1}{2}
  \qquad (|q| \approx 1).

The threading carries half the Alexander weight of the pairwise construction. This propagates into the crossing energy, halving the predicted ring-closure barrier.
